# Kspec Automation Session - Task Work

**Session ID:** `01KJPDHWGZQSSMPV34A1D7Q10X`
**Iteration:** 1 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)


### Current State

> **Truncated** (101330 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Agent Definition Schema
Type: feature
Description:
  Extend the existing AgentSchema in kynetic.meta.yaml with dispatch rules,
  adapter reference, skill configuration, budget/limit defaults, and
  concurrency settings. Each agent definition is a declarative description
  of when and how to spawn an ACP agent. Includes CLI commands for
  managing agent definitions (add, set, remove).
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: An agent definition exists in kynetic.meta.yaml with an adapter field

    When: The meta manifest is loaded and validated

    Then: The adapter field is accepted as a string — it may reference a
registered adapter or an ad-hoc npx package name, matching the
existing resolveAdapter behavior

  [ac-2]
    Given: An agent definition includes a dispatch array

    When: Each entry specifies an event type (task.ready, task.needs_work,
task.pending_review) and optional filters

    Then: The dispatch rules are parsed and validated by the Zod schema

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent definition includes filter objects in dispatch rules

    When: Filters specify automation status, tags, or priority constraints

    Then: Each filter field is validated independently against its expected
type (automation: string enum, tags: string array, priority: number)

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent definition includes budget fields (max_tasks, timeout_minutes)

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: Budget fields are accepted as optional positive numbers with no
required minimum

  [ac-5]
    Given: An agent definition includes a skills array referencing skill slugs

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: Skills are accepted as a string array — resolution happens at
dispatch time, not validation time

  [ac-6]
    Given: An agent definition includes concurrency settings (max_concurrent)

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: max_concurrent is accepted as a positive integer defaulting to 1

  [ac-7]
    Given: An agent definition includes an auto_approve boolean

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: auto_approve defaults to false when omitted

  [ac-8]
    Given: Existing agent definitions in meta lack the new dispatch/adapter fields

    When: The meta manifest is loaded

    Then: The schema validates successfully with all new fields using their
defaults (dispatch: [], adapter: undefined, skills: [],
budget: undefined, concurrency: {max_concurrent: 1},
auto_approve: false)

  [ac-9]
    Given: A user runs kspec meta add agent with required fields

    When: The command executes

    Then: A new agent definition is added to kynetic.meta.yaml with

    Given: A user runs kspec meta set agent <id> with updated fields

    When: The agent definition exists

    Then: The specified fields are updated while preserving unmodified fields

Extend the existing AgentSchema in kynetic.meta.yaml with dispatch rules,
adapter reference, skill configuration, budget/limit defaults, and
concurrency settings. Each agent definition is a declarative description
of when and how to spawn an ACP agent. Includes CLI commands for
managing agent definitions (add, set, remove).


Acceptance Criteria (11):
  [ac-1]
    Given: An agent definition exists in kynetic.meta.yaml with an adapter field

    When: The meta manifest is loaded and validated

    Then: The adapter field is accepted as a string — it may reference a
registered adapter or an ad-hoc npx package name, matching the
existing resolveAdapter behavior

  [ac-2]
    Given: An agent definition includes a dispatch array

    When: Each entry specifies an event type (task.ready, task.needs_work,
task.pending_review) and optional filters

    Then: The dispatch rules are parsed and validated by the Zod schema

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent definition includes filter objects in dispatch rules

    When: Filters specify automation status, tags, or priority constraints

    Then: Each filter field is validated independently against its expected
type (automation: string enum, tags: string array, priority: number)

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent definition includes budget fields (max_tasks, timeout_minutes)

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: Budget fields are accepted as optional positive numbers with no
required minimum

  [ac-5]
    Given: An agent definition includes a skills array referencing skill slugs

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: Skills are accepted as a string array — resolution happens at
dispatch time, not validation time

  [ac-6]
    Given: An agent definition includes concurrency settings (max_concurrent)

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: max_concurrent is accepted as a positive integer defaulting to 1

  [ac-7]
    Given: An agent definition includes an auto_approve boolean

    When: The schema is validated

    Then: auto_approve defaults to false when omitted

  [ac-8]
    Given: Existing agent definitions in meta lack the new dispatch/adapter fields

    When: The meta manifest is loaded

    Then: The schema validates successfully with all new fields using their
defaults (dispatch: [], adapter: undefined, skills: [],
budget: undefined, concurrency: {max_concurrent: 1},
auto_approve: false)

  [ac-9]
    Given: A user runs kspec meta add agent with required fields

    When: The command executes

    Then: A new agent definition is added to kynetic.meta.yaml with
a generated ULID and the provided configuration

  [ac-10]
    Given: A user runs kspec meta set agent <id> with updated fields

    When: The agent definition exists

    Then: The specified fields are updated while preserving unmodified fields

  [ac-11]
    Given: A user runs kspec meta remove agent <id>

    When: The agent definition exists

    Then: The agent definition is removed from kynetic.meta.yaml


Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N

ℹ Synced spec "Agent Definition Schema" implementation: not_started -> in_progress

**Session ID:** `01KJPDHWGZQSSMPV34A1D7Q10X`

> ```

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

    55→  close_reason: z.string().optional(),
    56→});

Implementing: Session Model Evolution

Extend SessionMetadata with trigger source, agent definition reference,
and structured completion tracking. Extend SessionStatusSchema with

  [ac-3]
    Given: SessionStatusSchema currently allows active, completed, abandoned

    When: The schema is extended

    Given: kspec session log show is run on a new-style invocation session

    When: The session contains agent.* events

the existing event display patterns

/**
 * Trigger source enum — what caused this agent session to be dispatched.
 * - manual: Started manually by user
 * - task.ready: Dispatched because a task became ready
 * - task.needs_work: Dispatched because a task needs work (fix cycle)
 * - task.pending_review: Dispatched for PR review
 * - legacy: Old ralph sessions without explicit trigger
 *
 * AC: @session-model-evolution ac-1, ac-2
 */
export const SessionTriggerSchema = z.enum([
  "manual",
  "task.ready",
  "task.needs_work",
  "task.pending_review",
  "legacy",
]);

export type SessionTrigger = z.infer<typeof SessionTriggerSchema>;

/**
 * Session metadata stored in session.yaml.
 * AC-5: includes task_id (optional), agent_type, status, started_at, ended_at
 */

/** Type of agent running the session */
  agent_type: z.string(),

  /**
   * Reference to the agent definition that dispatched this session.
   * For legacy sessions without this field, defaults to agent_type value.

  agent_id: z.string().optional(),

  trigger: SessionTriggerSchema.optional(),

Extend EventTypeSchema with agent.* event types

Update session log list rendering to show session type

Write tests for all 7 ACs

rawInput.command:
kspec task note @implement-session-model-evolution "Implemented all 7 ACs:
- ac-1/ac-2: Added trigger (enum: manual, task.ready, task.needs_work, task.pending_review, legacy) and agent_id fields to SessionMetadataSchema as optional fields. Updated createSession to pass them through. Backward compat: old sessions without these fields parse fine with undefined values.
- ac-3: Extended SessionStatusSchema with timed_out and failed. Updated statusCounts record in computeSessionLogStats to include new values.
- ac-4: Extended EventTypeSchema with agent.dispatched, agent.started, agent.completed, agent.failed, agent.timeout.
- ac-5: appendEvent accepts agent.completed with task_id, outcome, duration_ms payload (no schema enforcement on data - open object).
- ac-6: Added session_type field to SessionLogSummary and SessionLogDetail (loop vs invocation). resolveSessionType helper: trigger set and not 'legacy' → invocation, else → loop. Updated session log list to show Type column.
- ac-7: Updated summarizeEventData to render agent.* events with human-readable summaries. Updated event type color handling (magenta for agent.*). Added Type line to session log show metadata.
Files changed: src/sessions/types.ts, src/sessions/store.ts, src/cli/commands/session/log.ts
New test file: tests/session-model-evolution.test.ts (24 tests, all passing)
No regressions: 195 session tests pass, shard failures are pre-existing (enhanced-setup.test.ts)." 2>&1
